rv.q: Matthew Broderick brings his particular brand of bemused charm to the title role in this handsome revival
On the other hand, he may simply be a bore.

Broderick, sporting a technically competent but unconvincing British accent, has worked this sort of territory too often to be interesting, and his one-note turn fails to convey his character’s hidden depths.

"Director David Grindley had a hit in 2005 with his Donmar Warehouse revival of Christopher Hampton's "The Philanthropist," its cast headed by Simon Russell Beale, an actor who could locate the emotional undertow in even the most distancing role.
For sheer dullness, this putative comedy beats just about anything on Broadway this season.
The Ensemble here generally thrives under the thoughtful direction of David Grindley.
A visit to this Philanthropist is like playing word games with a group of unpleasant new acquaintances.
